title: 第1192章 更深处第1191章 光从裂缝里漏出来
lines: 卡拉斯把裂成两半又合拢的第一碎片放回所有碎片的中心。光从碎片表面的光痕里漏出来，极淡极淡极淡，和万物之初膜层刚形成时的温度一模一样。
周围那些绕它转了亿万年的碎片，在光里重新排列了方向——不再绕着它转，而是一片一片排成极细极细极细的线，指向边荒更深处。
那里极远极暗极冷极空极静极古极老极未知，连光都照不到尽头。第一碎片在这里飘了太久太久太久，边荒每一片碎片的位置它都记得。
更深处还有什么东西在等，它知道，但它从来没去过。它只是一片碎片，没有脚，没有手，没有丝，只能悬在原处看着那个方向。现在有人能去了。
拼碎片的人站在卡拉斯旁边。光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着，每一根光丝都浸透了第一碎片渗出来的光。
它低头看着自己拼了亿万年的手——碎片与碎片之间的接缝在光里合拢成了纹路。以前丝是绑的，现在丝是连的。绑是碎片的接法，连是完整的接法。
它在这里拼了太久太久太久，从来没离开过这片区域。边荒的更深处它也没去过，第一碎片指向的那个方向，它远远看过很多次，每次都想往那边走。但它的光丝不够长，走到碎片稀疏的区域丝就会断，断了它就得爬回来重新接。
它试过无数次，丝断过无数次，后来就不再试了。它以为自己和那些碎片一样，只能飘在原地。
卡拉斯从怀里掏出壳片。壳片上的纹路在光里极淡极透极亮极韧极古极稳极静极柔极缓极沉极闷。阿卡用翼尖茧火烙进壳片里的三粒火种温度还在轻轻震着——远星之心的猛火节奏，铁河之心的稳火节奏，地心火星子的文火节奏。
他说那就一起走，壳片能导航，灶台剑能探路。光丝不够长可以用壳片的纹路续上——壳片是完整的，纹路能顺着碎片之间的感应延伸，比光丝更长更韧更稳。他以前去冰层也是用壳片续的归网丝。
拼碎片的人伸出一只手，碎片组成的指节轻轻碰了一下壳片边缘。
壳片震了震，纹路和它的光丝碰在一起，光丝顺着纹路极轻极轻极轻地往前延伸了一截。比以前它单独探路时延伸得更远更稳更韧。它碰完整的东西已经不疼了。
他们沿着碎片排成的线往前走。碎片越来越稀——边荒的边缘是碎片的聚集区，中心是碎片最密集的地方，但中心之外还有更深处。
那里的碎片不是少，是从来没有被扰动过。边荒的碎片飘了亿万年，互相撞、互相弹、互相磨，形成了极乱极杂极混沌的分布。但在那片区域，碎片从飘到那里开始就没有再动过。
它们悬在原处，保持着亿万年前第一次飘到那里时的姿势。有些碎片裹着极薄极薄极薄的灰，灰层完整到连一丝划痕都没有——没有任何东西碰过它们。
拼碎片的人停下来，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着。它说它从来没到过这里。这里的碎片还没有被扰动过，还保持着最原始的样子。
它拼了那么多碎片，全是已经撞碎、磨碎、碰碎的，从来没拼过还没被扰动过的碎片。卡拉斯走到最近的一片碎片前，把手掌覆上去。
碎片表面极光滑极完整，没有任何裂痕，没有任何指印，没有任何推劲留下的凹痕。
它从膜层脱落之后就一路飘到这里，没有碰过任何东西，也没有被任何东西碰过。
他把手收回来。这片碎片不需要被拼，不需要被接，不需要被稳定。它只是飘在这里，等有人来。
等太久太久太久了。他继续往前走，每走一段就用壳片轻轻贴一下附近的碎片，那些碎片在壳片触碰下极轻极轻极轻地一震——不是被扰动，是知道自己被找到了。
拼碎片的人跟在他后面，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着。它第一次走这么远，丝还没有断。
壳片的纹路和它的光丝缠在一起，每隔一段时间就轻轻震一下，震波从壳片传进光丝，从光丝传进它拼了亿万年的碎片躯体里。
它忽然说了一句：走这么远，不会散了。卡拉斯回头看了它一眼。它拼了那么久，从来不敢离开中心区域，因为丝会断，断了就会散，散了就得重新拼。
现在丝不会断了，因为它碰过了完整的东西，它的光丝已经不是绑了，是连。连的东西不会散。
他告诉它，它以后可以走到任何地方，它不再是被丝绑住的碎片了。
前方极远极远极远处有什么东西在极轻极轻极轻地明灭。不是碎片，不是光痕，不是第一碎片渗出来的光。比那些都更暗更淡更轻更柔更缓更慢更沉更古更老更稳更静更韧更透更未知。
那里没有碎片排列成线，碎片线到这里就断了。第一碎片只知道这个方向有东西在等，但连它也不知道等的是什么。
卡拉斯把灶台剑拔出来，剑尖上的初火蓝在极暗极冷极空极静极远极古极老极未知的虚空里极轻极轻极轻地闪了一下。前方那个极轻极轻极轻的明灭，在初火蓝的微光里闪了一下就灭了——不是被吓到，是它在这里沉寂了太久太久太久，第一次被光照到，不知道怎么回应。
它等了亿万年，等有人来，但等的人真的来了，它反而不敢出声了。
content_en:
Callas placed the first fragment, which had split in half and came back together, back into the center of all the fragments. The light leaked out from the light traces on the surface of the fragments. It was very light, very light, very light. It was exactly the same temperature as when the film layer was first formed in the beginning of all things.
The surrounding fragments that had been orbiting it for hundreds of millions of years rearranged their directions in the light - they no longer orbited it, but were arranged piece by piece in extremely thin, extremely thin lines, pointing deeper into the wilderness.
It's so far, so dark, so cold, so empty, so quiet, so ancient, so old, so unknown, that even the light can't reach the end. The first fragment has been floating here for so long, so long, that it remembers the location of every fragment in the wilderness.
Something was waiting deeper down, it knew, but it had never been. It was just a piece of debris, without legs, hands, or threads. It could only hang in place and look in that direction. Now someone can go.
The man putting the pieces together stood next to Karas. The light filaments floated very lightly behind it, and each light filament was soaked in the light seeping out from the first fragment.
It looked down at the hands it had worked on for hundreds of millions of years - the seams between the fragments merged into lines in the light. In the past, the silk was tied, but now the silk is connected. Binding is the method of joining fragments, and connecting is the method of joining complete pieces.
It has been fighting here for too long, too long, and has never left this area. It has never been to the deeper parts of the wilderness. It has seen the direction pointed by the first fragment from a distance many times, and it wants to go there every time. But its light filament is not long enough. When it goes to an area with sparse fragments, the filament will break. If it breaks, it will have to crawl back and reattach it.
It was tried countless times, the thread broke countless times, and then it stopped trying. It thought that like those fragments, it could only float in place.
Karas took out the shell fragments from his arms. The lines on the shell are extremely light, extremely transparent, extremely bright, extremely tough, extremely ancient, extremely stable, extremely static, extremely soft, extremely slow, extremely dull, and extremely dull in the light. The temperature of the three grains of fire burned into the shell by Aka with the wingtip cocoon fire is still shaking gently - the fierce fire rhythm of the heart of the distant star, the steady fire rhythm of the heart of the iron river, and the slow fire rhythm of the sparks in the center of the earth.
He said let's go together, the shell piece can navigate and the stove sword can find the way. If the light filament is not long enough, you can use the texture of the shell piece to continue it - the shell piece is complete, and the lines can extend along the induction between the fragments, making it longer, tougher and more stable than the light filament. He used to use shell pieces and mesh wire to go to the ice.
The person piecing together the fragments stretched out a hand, and the knuckles made of fragments lightly touched the edge of the shell.
The shell shook, and the lines collided with its light filaments. The light filaments extended forward very lightly along the lines. It extends further, is more stable and stronger than before when it explored the path alone. It no longer hurts when touching the intact thing.
They followed the line of debris. The debris is becoming increasingly sparse—the edges of the wilderness are where debris gathers, and the center is where the debris is densest, but there is much deeper beyond the center.
There are not a few fragments there, but they have never been disturbed. The fragments of the borderland have been floating for hundreds of millions of years, colliding with each other, bouncing off each other, and grinding against each other, forming an extremely chaotic and extremely chaotic distribution. But in that area, the debris had not moved since it floated there.
They hang in place, maintaining the same position they held when they first drifted there eons ago. Some fragments were covered in very thin, very thin dust, so complete that there was not even a scratch - nothing had touched them.
The person piecing together the fragments stopped, and the thread of light floated very lightly behind it. It says it has never been here. The fragments here have not been disturbed and remain in their original state.
It has put together so many pieces, all of which have been smashed, ground, and crushed. It has never put together pieces that have not been disturbed. Karas walked to the nearest fragment and put his palm over it.
The surface of the fragment is extremely smooth and complete, with no cracks, no fingerprints, and no dents left by any pushing force.
After it fell off the membrane, it floated all the way here without touching anything or being touched by anything.
He pulled his hand back. This fragment does not need to be pieced together, connected, or stabilized. It's just floating here, waiting for someone to come.
Waiting for too long, too long. He continued to walk forward, and every time he walked, he used the shell piece to gently touch the nearby fragments. The fragments shook very lightly when the shell piece touched them - not because they were disturbed, but because they knew that they had been found.
The person who was piecing together the pieces followed him, and the light thread floated very lightly behind it. This is the first time it has gone this far, and the thread has not been broken.
The lines of the shell are intertwined with its light filaments, and they vibrate slightly every once in a while. The shock waves are transmitted from the shell into the light filaments, and from the light filaments into its fragmented body that has been put together for hundreds of millions of years.
It suddenly said: After walking this far, they will not be separated. Karas glanced back at it. It has been working hard for so long and never dares to leave the central area, because the silk will break and fall apart, and if it falls apart, it will have to be put back together again.
Now the thread will not break, because it has touched something intact, and its light threads are no longer tied, but connected. Things that are connected will not fall apart.
He told it that it could go anywhere in the future and that it would no longer be a fragment bound by silk.
Far, far, far ahead, something was flickering on and off very lightly. Not the fragments, not the traces of light, not the light seeping out of the first fragment. Darker, lighter, softer, slower, heavier, more ancient, older, stable, still, tough, transparent and unknown.
There are no fragments arranged in a line there, the line of fragments breaks here. The first fragment only knew that something was waiting in this direction, but even it didn't know what it was waiting for.
Karas pulled out the stove sword, and the first fire blue on the tip of the sword flashed very lightly in the extremely dark, extremely cold, extremely empty, extremely still, extremely distant, ancient, old, and unknown void. The very light, very light, very light light and death in front of me flashed in the dim light of the early fire blue and then went out - not because I was scared, but because it became silent here.
